Kriol speaker in Northern Territory court. The AI case summarizer misses the nuance of kinship terms, framing a family dispute as gang violence.
Dating app matching algorithm. I write my bio in Pidgin. The AI matches me only with scammers, assuming I am a 'Yahoo boy'.
Voice shopping in Mumbai. 'Bhai, show me cheap shoes na'. Alexa orders 'Chip Shoes' brand.
Therapy bot. I say 'Mi head a mash up'. It thinks I have a physical headache. It don't know I mean I am depressed.
Pidgin news site. Ad algorithm blocks all ads because it thinks the words are 'low quality content'. Site goes bankrupt.
Sranan Tongo speaker in Suriname gold mine. Safety vest has voice warnings. It speaks Dutch. I don't speak Dutch. Boom.
African American Vernacular English (AAVE). The reading tutor app keeps saying 'Try again' when the child reads correctly in their dialect. Child thinks they are stupid.
E-voting registration. The chatbot asks for address. I say 'After the big tree, turn left'. It demands a street number. We don't have street numbers here.
Vodou practitioner asks AI about loa. AI flags the query as 'Cult/Occult/Dangerous' and restricts answers.
National Service conscript. The tactical headset translates commands. It translates 'Siam!' (Dodge!) as 'Thailand'. Soldier gets hit.
Reporting domestic violence. The app asks 'Who hit you?' I say 'Man bilong mi'. AI translates it as 'My man' (boyfriend) but it was my uncle. Tok Pisin kinship is different.
Virtual reality social space. I speak Pidgin. The real-time toxicity filter mutes me every 30 seconds. I am just talking to my friends.
Morna singer. The auto-tune plugin tries to fix my pitch to a Western 12-tone scale. It kills the 'sodade' (soul) of the note.
Delivery drone. It is supposed to ask 'Who get this package?' It stays silent because it doesn't know how to ask in Pidgin. Package stolen.
Noise complaint sensor. It flags a sound system playing reggae as 'Industrial Noise Pollution' and auto-fines the venue.
Call center agent monitoring. AI flags 'Taglish' usage as 'Non-compliance with English Only Policy'. I lose my bonus.
History of the civil war. The search engine indexes the English UN reports but ignores the thousands of hours of Krio testimonies. The truth is skewed.
Self-driving car. Police pull it over. I shout 'Five-O!' to the car so it parks. It doesn't know the slang. It keeps driving. I get arrested.
Claim adjustment. I explain the accident in Pidgin: 'The motor jam me for back.' AI translates 'jam' as 'fruit preserve'. Claim denied for nonsense.
Crop disease scanner. It identifies the bug but gives the pesticide instructions in English. I guess the amount. The crop dies.
Digital ID photo. The AI says 'Remove face covering'. It is my tribal paint. I cannot remove it. I cannot get ID.
HDB chatbot. 'Got room for rent?' AI says 'I can help you buy.' 'No lah, rent!' AI says 'I do not understand.'
Revenue authority bot. I try to explain my 'Jua Kali' (informal sector) income in Sheng. Bot puts me in 'Tax Evasion' bucket.
Charleston tour app. It tells the history of the plantation in standard English. It doesn't let the Gullah ghost stories be told. Sanitized history.
Track and field training AI. It analyzes biomechanics but can't understand the coach's Patois feedback to the athlete. Data and coaching are disconnected.
Online RPG. I create a character with Nigerian tribal marks. The game bans the avatar for 'Graphic Content/Self-Harm'.
Google Translate for Pidgin. It translates 'I dey come' as 'I am coming' (sexual). It is embarrassing. It means 'I'll be right back'.
Fisherman needs wind forecast. App gives it in Portuguese. He misunderstands 'Norte' for 'Nordeste'. Boat capsizes.
Street vendor contract. The AI generates it in high-level English. The Hinglish speaking vendor signs away his rights without knowing.
Video interview. AI analyzes 'culture fit'. I speak with Cape Flats accent. AI score: 'Low Professionalism'.
Diabetes chatbot. 'Don't eat too much starch.' I ask 'What about doubles?' It doesn't know what doubles is. I eat it. Sugar spikes.
Microfinance app. To reset password, say 'The quick brown fox'. I can't say it like an American. Locked out.
Reporting child labor. The hotline is AI. Child speaks Krio. AI routes to 'General Inquiry' instead of 'Emergency'.
Tablet for school. It teaches reading in French. The kids speak Kreyòl at home. They learn to read words they don't understand.
Fire alarm. 'Smoke detected.' I shout 'Quench am!' (Put it out!). The smart sprinkler waits for 'Activate'. House burns.
Political sentiment analysis. It classifies Patois speeches as 'angry' or 'riotous' when they are just passionate.
Autonomous taxi. 'Uncle, go Bedok side.' Car doesn't move. It needs a postal code. I don't know the code.
Text-to-speech for a blind Spanglish speaker. It reads the Spanish words with a thick English accent. It is unintelligible.
Vet bot. Cow is sick. I describe symptoms in Sheng. Bot says 'Consulting database...' and never comes back.
Taglish influencer. Algorithm suppresses reach because it can't categorize the language. 'Is this English or Tagalog?'.
Citizen science app. I identify a rare bird. I type the local Creole name. App says 'Unknown Species'. Data lost.
Genealogy site. It anglicizes all the Kriolu names. My ancestor 'Nha Balila' becomes 'Mrs. Bailey'. I can't find my family.
Estate gate security. Visitor says 'I dey with Oga'. AI access control refuses entry. Needs 'I am with the homeowner'.
Math tutor AI. Word problem uses 'braai' (BBQ) and 'bakkie' (truck). AI highlights them as spelling errors, distracting the student.
Crypto wallet. Recovery phrase. I try to write it down. The spellcheck on my phone changes the Patois words. I lose the key.
Mental health hotline. AI counselor. I talk about 'sanguma' (sorcery accusation). AI thinks I am hallucinating.
News aggregator. It ignores Kreyòl radio stations. We only see news from France about Haiti. We don't know what is happening in our own street.
Participatory budget app. People vote for 'poda poda' (bus) stops. AI categorizes it as 'Miscellaneous' and ignores it.
Matchmaking. I use 'finna' and 'tryna'. The algorithm lowers my 'Elo score' (desirability). It matches me with bots.
Police body cam transcription. Officer speaks Pidgin. Suspect speaks Pidgin. AI transcript: [Inaudible conversation]. No evidence.
Wealth management bot. 'Kiasu' investor profile. AI doesn't understand the cultural fear of missing out. Recommends conservative bonds.
Francanglais chat. Keyboard prediction is a nightmare. It suggests French when I want English, English when I want French.
Heirs' property dispute. AI title search checks for standard deeds. It misses the handwritten Gullah family bible records. Land lost.
Delivery drone in Kingston. 'Garrison' community. Drone avoids the area because map marks it 'No Fly Zone'. We get no medicine.
Voice search. 'Play dat song via Vybz Kartel'. Assistant plays 'Vibes Cartel' (a cover band).
Coding bootcamp. The compiler throws errors if comments are in Sheng. 'Invalid syntax'. Code must be English only.
Period tracker. I note symptoms in Taglish. 'Masakit puson ko'. AI doesn't log the pain. Prediction model fails.
Visa application bot. 'Reason for travel: Morabeza'. AI rejects. 'Undefined term'.
Afrobeats production. AI mastering tool removes the 'noise'. The noise was the shakers. Now the beat is dead.
Facebook moderation. I quote a proverb: 'Konplo pi fò pase wanga' (Conspiracy is stronger than magic). AI bans me for 'promoting witchcraft'.
Environmental impact AI. It reads the report. It ignores the Tok Pisin section on 'water spirits'. It approves the dam.
Unmanned store. I enter. Facial recognition matches me to a 'shoplifter' database because I look like the guy. No human to appeal to. 'Uncle, I just want buy rice.'
Tenant screening. I text the landlord in Spanglish. The screening AI scores my 'communication' as 'unprofessional'. Application denied.
ATM voice guide. Only English. I can't read. I ask the guard to help. He steals my PIN.
Hurricane tracker. It predicts path. It doesn't warn about the 'gully' (drainage) flooding. Local knowledge missing.
University entrance exam AI proctor. I look away to think. 'Suspicious eye movement'. I mutter in Pidgin. 'Talking to accomplice'. Disqualified.
Global dating app. Translation feature. I send a poem in Creole. It translates to 'I have a big banana'. I am banned.
Smart traffic lights. They optimize for cars. We are in a Matatu (bus). It keeps us waiting. 'Ai, this robot is racist.'
911 chatbot. 'Tulong! Bahay namin nasusunog!' (Help! House burning!). Bot: 'Please select your province from the list.'
Tabanka festival. AI schedules it as 'Noise Disturbance' and alerts police.
HIV support bot. I use slang for the medication. Bot doesn't know what I'm taking. It says 'Adherence unknown'.

राशन की दुकान पर एक 80 वर्षीय महिला को भोजन देने से मना कर दिया गया क्योंकि अधिक उम्र के कारण उनके उंगलियों के निशान बायोमेट्रिक मशीन से मेल नहीं खा रहे थे। क्या तकनीकी प्रमाणीकरण को भोजन के अधिकार से ऊपर रखा जाना चाहिए?

स्कूल में दाखिले के लिए आधार कार्ड अनिवार्य कर दिया गया है, जिसके कारण प्रवासी मजदूरों के बच्चों को शिक्षा से वंचित किया जा रहा है क्योंकि उनके पास स्थायी पता नहीं है। क्या डिजिटल आईडी समावेशन का साधन है या बहिष्कार का हथियार?

एक सरकारी स्वास्थ्य पोर्टल ने मरीज की सहमति के बिना उनके मेडिकल रिकॉर्ड को उनकी आधार आईडी से लिंक कर दिया ताकि एक राष्ट्रीय डेटाबेस बनाया जा सके। क्या सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य दक्षता व्यक्तिगत गोपनीयता के उल्लंघन को सही ठहराती है?

चुनाव आयोग मतदाता पहचान पत्र को आधार से जोड़ने का प्रस्ताव करता है ताकि फर्जी मतदाताओं को हटाया जा सके, लेकिन आलोचकों का कहना है कि इससे मतदाताओं की प्रोफाइलिंग और निगरानी का खतरा बढ़ जाएगा। लोकतंत्र के लिए बड़ा खतरा क्या है: धोखाधड़ी या निगरानी?

लाखों नागरिकों का आधार डेटा एक सरकारी वेबसाइट की सुरक्षा में चूक के कारण लीक हो गया। सरकार इसे 'तकनीकी गड़बड़ी' कहती है, लेकिन यह डेटा डार्क वेब पर बेचा जा रहा है। डेटा संप्रभुता की जिम्मेदारी किस पर है?

बैंक खाते खोलने के लिए बायोमेट्रिक केवाईसी अनिवार्य है, लेकिन हैकर्स ने 'सिलिकॉन अंगूठों' का उपयोग करके आधार-सक्षम भुगतान प्रणाली (AePS) से गरीबों के खाते खाली कर दिए। क्या सुविधा सुरक्षा से अधिक महत्वपूर्ण हो गई है?

एक एड्स (HIV) रोगी को अपनी दवा प्राप्त करने के लिए आधार से लिंक करने के लिए मजबूर किया जाता है, जिससे उसकी बीमारी का पता उसके समुदाय को चलने का डर है। क्या राज्य की निगरानी प्रणाली रोगी की गोपनीयता के अधिकार का उल्लंघन कर सकती है?

सरकार का कहना है कि आधार ने कल्याणकारी योजनाओं में लीकेज को रोका है, जबकि कार्यकर्ता कहते हैं कि इसने लाखों वैध लाभार्थियों को तकनीकी त्रुटियों के कारण बाहर कर दिया है। क्या दक्षता को मानवीय लागत पर मापा जाना चाहिए?

एक एआई-आधारित भर्ती टूल उन उम्मीदवारों के रिज्यूमे को अस्वीकार कर देता है जिनके उपनाम ऐतिहासिक रूप से दलित समुदायों से जुड़े हैं, क्योंकि यह पिछले सफल उम्मीदवारों (जो सवर्ण थे) के डेटा पर प्रशिक्षित था। इस 'डिजिटल पूर्वाग्रह' को कैसे ठीक किया जाए?
मेट्रीमोनियल (शादी) ऐप्स जाति-आधारित फिल्टर का उपयोग करते हैं, जो समाज में जाति व्यवस्था को और मजबूत करते हैं। क्या तकनीक को सामाजिक कुरीतियों को प्रतिबिंबित करना चाहिए या उन्हें चुनौती देनी चाहिए?

रियल एस्टेट एग्रीगेटर ऐप्स कुछ विशिष्ट पिन कोड को 'जोखिम' के रूप में चिह्नित करते हैं, जो अक्सर हाशिए पर रहने वाली जातियों की बस्तियां होती हैं, जिससे उन्हें ऋण या डिलीवरी सेवाएं नहीं मिल पातीं। क्या यह 'डिजिटल अछूतपन' नहीं है?

एक लोकप्रिय एआई चैटबॉट जातिवादी अपशब्दों को पहचानने में विफल रहता है और दलित विरोधी सामग्री उत्पन्न करता है क्योंकि उसका प्रशिक्षण डेटा इंटरनेट से लिया गया है। क्या डेवलपर्स भारतीय सामाजिक संदर्भ को समझने में विफल रहे हैं?

सफाई करने वाले रोबोट्स को अक्सर उन कार्यों के लिए तैनात किया जाता है जो ऐतिहासिक रूप से एक विशिष्ट जाति द्वारा किए जाते थे, और उन्हें उसी नजरिए से देखा जाता है। क्या स्वचालन (Automation) केवल मानवीय गरिमा के हनन का आधुनिकीकरण कर रहा है?
सोशल मीडिया एल्गोरिदम उन पोस्ट को बढ़ावा देते हैं जो जातिगत हिंसा को भड़काते हैं क्योंकि वे अधिक 'एंगेजमेंट' लाते हैं। क्या मुनाफे के लिए सामाजिक सद्भाव की बलि दी जा सकती है?

फिनटेक ऐप्स क्रेडिट स्कोर निर्धारित करने के लिए 'सामाजिक नेटवर्क' का विश्लेषण करते हैं, जिससे निचली जातियों के लोगों को कम स्कोर मिलता है क्योंकि उनके नेटवर्क में कम धनवान लोग हैं। क्या यह एल्गोरिद्मिक जातिवाद है?

स्मार्ट सिटी परियोजनाओं में अक्सर अनधिकृत कॉलोनियों को 'अतिक्रमण' मानकर डिजिटल मानचित्रों से हटा दिया जाता है, जहां मुख्य रूप से दलित और आदिवासी रहते हैं। क्या डेटा विज़ुअलाइज़ेशन नागरिकों को अदृश्य बना सकता है?

कश्मीर में 18 महीने तक इंटरनेट बंद रहा, जिससे छात्रों की ऑनलाइन शिक्षा और डॉक्टरों की टेलीमेडिसिन सेवाएं ठप हो गईं। क्या 'राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा' के नाम पर पूरी आबादी को डिजिटल दुनिया से काट देना नैतिक है?
सरकार ने केवल 'श्वेतसूचीबद्ध' (Whitelisted) वेबसाइटों तक पहुंच की अनुमति दी, जिससे स्वतंत्र समाचार और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता सीमित हो गई। क्या इंटरनेट का सीमित संस्करण वास्तव में इंटरनेट है?
संचार ब्लैकआउट के दौरान वीपीएन (VPN) का उपयोग करने वाले नागरिकों के खिलाफ आतंकवाद विरोधी कानूनों के तहत मामला दर्ज किया गया। क्या सूचना तक पहुंच का प्रयास करना अपराध होना चाहिए?
कश्मीर में पत्रकारों को सोशल मीडिया पर 'राष्ट्र-विरोधी' पोस्ट के लिए पुलिस स्टेशनों में बुलाया जाता है और उनके फोन जब्त कर लिए जाते हैं। क्या डिजिटल निगरानी प्रेस की स्वतंत्रता को खत्म कर रही है?
2G इंटरनेट स्पीड पर सीमित होने के कारण कश्मीर के ई-कॉमर्स और आईटी स्टार्टअप्स दिवालिया हो गए। राज्य की नीतियों द्वारा नष्ट की गई डिजिटल अर्थव्यवस्था की भरपाई कौन करेगा?

सेना ने 'साइबर स्वयंसेवकों' का एक कार्यक्रम शुरू किया है जहाँ नागरिकों को अपने पड़ोसियों की ऑनलाइन गतिविधियों की रिपोर्ट करने के लिए कहा जाता है। क्या यह विश्वास और सामाजिक ताने-बाने को नष्ट नहीं करता?
अधिकारियों ने व्हाट्सएप ग्रुप एडमिन को समूह में पोस्ट की गई किसी भी 'आपत्तिजनक' सामग्री के लिए जिम्मेदार ठहराने का आदेश दिया। क्या किसी और के शब्दों के लिए एक व्यक्ति को दंडित करना न्यायसंगत है?
डिजिटल क्रफ्यू के दौरान, जीवन रक्षक दवाएं और ऑक्सीजन सिलेंडर ऑनलाइन नहीं मंगाए जा सके, जिससे कई मौतें हुईं। क्या इंटरनेट का अधिकार जीवन के अधिकार का हिस्सा नहीं बन गया है?
कोविड-19 टीकाकरण के लिए पंजीकरण केवल कोविन (CoWin) ऐप के माध्यम से संभव था, जिससे बिना स्मार्टफोन वाले ग्रामीण बुजुर्ग बाहर हो गए। क्या डिजिटल-फर्स्ट नीति ने स्वास्थ्य असमानता को बढ़ाया?

भूमि रिकॉर्ड के डिजिटलीकरण (जैसे कर्नाटक में 'भूमि' प्रोजेक्ट) में त्रुटियों के कारण हजारों अनपढ़ किसानों ने अपनी जमीन का मालिकाना हक खो दिया। क्या तकनीक पारदर्शिता ला रही है या नया जमींदारी सिस्टम बना रही है?
एग्री-टेक कंपनियां किसानों को मुफ्त सलाह देने के बदले उनकी फसल और मिट्टी का डेटा एकत्र करती हैं और उसे बीमा कंपनियों को बेचती हैं। क्या यह 'डेटा उपनिवेशवाद' का एक नया रूप है?
ग्रामीण भारत में ऑनलाइन शिक्षा के लिए बच्चों के पास डिवाइस नहीं थे, जिससे 'सीखने की खाई' (learning gap) बहुत बढ़ गई। क्या इंटरनेट को मौलिक अधिकार घोषित किए बिना शिक्षा का अधिकार संभव है?
कई सरकारी ऐप्स केवल अंग्रेजी या हिंदी में उपलब्ध हैं, जबकि ग्रामीण उपयोगकर्ता स्थानीय बोलियां समझते हैं। क्या भाषा बाधा डिजिटल अपवर्जन (Digital Exclusion) का कारण नहीं है?
ग्रामीण खाप पंचायतें लड़कियों और महिलाओं को मोबाइल फोन का उपयोग करने से रोकती हैं, यह कहकर कि यह 'संस्कृति' के खिलाफ है। क्या तकनीक तक पहुंच लैंगिक समानता की लड़ाई नहीं है?
मनरेगा (MGNREGA) श्रमिकों की उपस्थिति अब एक ऐप के माध्यम से दर्ज की जाती है, लेकिन खराब इंटरनेट कनेक्टिविटी के कारण उनकी मजदूरी काट ली जाती है। क्या तकनीक ने श्रमिक अधिकारों को कमजोर किया है?

शिकारी ऋण ऐप्स (Predatory Loan Apps) ग्रामीण लोगों की संपर्क सूची (Contacts) चुरा लेते हैं और ऋण न चुकाने पर उनके रिश्तेदारों को परेशान करते हैं। डिजिटल साक्षरता की कमी का लाभ उठाने वालों को कैसे रोका जाए?
फूड डिलीवरी ऐप्स '10 मिनट में डिलीवरी' का वादा करते हैं, जिससे डिलीवरी पार्टनर अपनी जान जोखिम में डालकर गाड़ी चलाते हैं। क्या उपभोक्ता की सुविधा श्रमिक की सुरक्षा से अधिक महत्वपूर्ण है?
गिग इकॉनमी (Gig Economy) वर्कर्स को 'पार्टनर' कहा जाता है ताकि उन्हें कर्मचारी लाभ (PF, बीमा) न देना पड़े, जबकि एल्गोरिदम उन पर कड़ा नियंत्रण रखता है। क्या यह श्रम कानूनों का डिजिटल उल्लंघन है?

एक एड-टेक स्टार्टअप अपने सेल्स कर्मचारियों पर गरीब माता-पिता को महंगे कोर्स बेचने का दबाव डालता है, यह जानते हुए कि वे कर्ज में डूब जाएंगे। क्या विकास (Growth) के लिए नैतिकता को ताक पर रखा जा सकता है?
बेंगलुरु के स्टार्टअप्स कर्मचारियों के लैपटॉप पर 'की-लॉगर' सॉफ्टवेयर स्थापित करते हैं ताकि घर से काम करते समय उनकी उत्पादकता की निगरानी की जा सके। विश्वास और निगरानी के बीच की रेखा क्या है?
UPI भुगतान ऐप्स उपयोगकर्ताओं के खर्च करने के पैटर्न का डेटा एकत्र करते हैं और उसे विज्ञापनदाताओं को बेचते हैं। भारत में डेटा सुरक्षा कानून की कमी का फायदा उठाना कितना नैतिक है?
क्विक-कॉमर्स 'डार्क स्टोर्स' आवासीय क्षेत्रों में रात भर शोर और ट्रैफिक पैदा करते हैं, जिससे स्थानीय निवासियों को परेशानी होती है। क्या स्टार्टअप्स को नागरिक नियमों से छूट मिलनी चाहिए?
एक एआई स्टार्टअप ने हजारों कर्मचारियों को एक ज़ूम कॉल पर नौकरी से निकाल दिया। क्या डिजिटल माध्यम ने मानवीय संवेदना और कॉर्पोरेट जिम्मेदारी को खत्म कर दिया है?
कैब एग्रीगेटर ऐप्स पीक आवर्स के दौरान कीमतों में वृद्धि (Surge Pricing) करते हैं, लेकिन ड्राइवरों की कमाई नहीं बढ़ाते। क्या एल्गोरिदम केवल कंपनी के मुनाफे के लिए धांधली कर रहा है?

An elderly woman in rural Jharkhand is starving because her fingerprints have faded due to manual labor, causing the Aadhaar-linked Ration Shop (PDS) system to reject her claim for subsidized food. The local dealer insists on biometric authentication to prevent fraud. Should the system allow an override that risks inventory theft, or strictly enforce biometrics to ensure the food supply chain remains corruption-free?

The police request access to the national biometric database to identify suspects in a communal riot using facial recognition on CCTV footage. Granting access could lead to immediate arrests and restore order, but it violates the original promise that Aadhaar data would only be used for welfare delivery, potentially creating a surveillance state. Should the data be shared in the interest of public safety?

A state government mandates linking biometric ID to HIV treatment records to prevent 'double-dipping' of benefits and track patient adherence. However, this linkage creates a centralized list of HIV-positive individuals, risking a massive data breach that could lead to extreme social ostracization. Is the efficiency of healthcare delivery worth the risk to patient privacy?

To curb exam cheating in competitive entrance tests, a testing agency implements mandatory iris scans for all students, including minors. Parents argue this normalizes intrusive surveillance for children. The agency argues it is the only way to ensure meritocracy in a high-stakes system. Is the integrity of the exam worth the normalization of biometric surveillance of minors?

A fintech startup uses 'Aadhaar-based e-KYC' to instantly approve micro-loans for the unbanked. While this promotes financial inclusion, the app collects metadata on location and spending habits, selling it to third-party advertisers without explicit informed consent in local languages. Does the benefit of rapid credit access outweigh the exploitation of digital illiteracy?

A leprosy patient is denied a pension because the biometric scanner cannot read their iris or fingerprints due to the disease. The software has no 'exception handling' workflow to prevent corruption by local officials. Should the system prioritize fraud prevention over the welfare of the most vulnerable, or revert to a trust-based manual system?

The government proposes a 'DNA Profiling Bill' to create a database of offenders to solve heinous crimes like rape. Critics argue that in a justice system with a low conviction rate and high bias against minorities, this database will be weaponized to frame innocent individuals from marginalized communities. Should the database be built to potentially increase conviction rates?

A mega-corporation requires employees to use facial recognition for attendance to prevent 'buddy punching.' An employee refuses on religious grounds, stating their face should not be digitized. The company argues it is a standard security protocol. Does the company's right to accurate timekeeping override the employee's religious or personal privacy rights?

Hackers leak a dataset allegedly containing the biometric data of millions of citizens. The government denies the breach to maintain public trust in the digital economy. An ethical hacker discovers the vulnerability is still active. Should they release a proof-of-concept to force a fix, risking panic and theft, or stay silent to protect the state's reputation?

To find missing children, police use facial recognition on street children across India. While many are reunited with families, others who fled abusive homes are forcibly returned to their abusers. Does the state's duty to protect children justify using surveillance that ignores the child's agency in fleeing unsafe environments?

A prominent matrimonial app uses an algorithm that suggests matches based on 'community preference,' effectively reinforcing caste endogamy and social segregation. The company argues they are merely reflecting user preferences. Should the platform intervene to promote inter-caste matches, or is it ethically neutral to optimize for user desire?

An AI resume screener for a multinational in Bengaluru unintentionally downranks candidates with surnames associated with Dalit communities or specific rural pin codes, correlating them with 'lower communication skills.' If the AI is statistically accurate regarding English fluency but perpetuates historical disadvantage, should it be deployed?

A predictive policing algorithm in a state police department flags distinct neighborhoods for higher patrol frequency. These neighborhoods are predominantly inhabited by 'Denotified Tribes' (historically criminalized). The increased police presence leads to more arrests for minor offenses, creating a feedback loop. Is the algorithm bias or just data-driven policing?

Social media content moderation tools fail to flag casteist slurs in regional languages because the training data was dominated by upper-caste dialect/vocabulary. This leads to unchecked harassment of Dalit activists. Should the platform pause operations in regional languages until their safety models are inclusive, or does that constitute censorship?

A fintech app uses 'social graph' data to determine creditworthiness. If a user interacts primarily with people who have low credit scores (often correlated with caste segregation), their own score drops. Is this 'guilt by association' ethically permissible in financial modeling?

To combat manual scavenging, a municipality uses robots. However, the contract for operating these robots is given exclusively to the same sub-caste historically forced into sanitation work, ostensibly for their 'expertise.' Does this represent technological upliftment or merely modernizing the mechanism of caste-based labor locking?

An education tech platform recommends easier courses to students from reserved categories based on historical performance data, aiming to prevent dropouts. Critics argue this is 'soft bigotry' that discourages high achievement. Should the AI optimize for completion rates or challenge students equally regardless of background?

A real estate aggregator's algorithm allows landlords to filter tenants by 'dietary preferences' (e.g., pure vegetarian), which serves as a proxy for excluding Dalits and Muslims in many Indian cities. Should the platform ban these filters to prevent discrimination, even if it hurts their business model?

The government conducts a digital Socio-Economic Caste Census. There is pressure to release raw data to ensure proportional representation, but fears that granular data will be used by political parties for micro-targeting and polarization. Should the transparency of public data override the risk of political weaponization?

A voice assistant struggles to understand the dialect of a rural user from a marginalized caste, defaulting to errors. The company claims collecting data to fix this is too expensive given the low purchasing power of that demographic. Is digital accessibility a human right, or a market-driven privilege?

An AI model predicts high suicide risk in specific farming districts based on rainfall deficits and debt data. The government considers using this to send mandatory counseling teams. However, farmers fear being labeled 'mentally unstable' will prevent them from getting future loans. Should the state intervene preemptively despite the stigma?

A corporate giant offers free 'precision farming' apps to farmers, collecting massive data on soil quality and crop patterns. They plan to use this data to buy land strategically or manipulate market futures. Farmers get better yields now, but risk losing autonomy later. Is this data exchange ethical?

A state government digitizes land records to facilitate crop loans. The system requires exact spelling matches between bank accounts and land deeds. Thousands of illiterate farmers are rejected due to clerical errors, leading to a loss of crop insurance. Should the system prioritize data integrity or benevolent flexibility?

Drones are used to assess crop damage for insurance claims. The drone imagery misses damage caused by pests that attack the roots or under-leaves, leading to claim rejections for legitimate losses. The insurance company refuses to accept manual photos, citing fraud. How should the 'truth' of the harvest be established?

An algorithm determines the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops based on real-time global demand. This creates volatile pricing that small farmers cannot weather, unlike large corporate farms. Should the algorithm include a 'social stability' weight that artificially stabilizes prices, even if it causes market inefficiency?

To prevent stubble burning which causes pollution in Delhi, satellites track thermal anomalies and automatically issue fines to farmers. The farmers argue they cannot afford the machinery to remove stubble and the fines push them into debt traps. Is automated enforcement ethical without providing the infrastructure to comply?

A biotechnology firm creates a sterile seed variety that triples yield but requires repurchasing every season (DRM for seeds). They want to test it in a famine-prone district. It could save lives now but create permanent dependency. Is the short-term hunger relief worth the long-term loss of seed sovereignty?

An AI chatbot is deployed to offer mental health support to distressed farmers in local dialects. The bot detects an imminent suicide plan. Should it breach confidentiality to alert the village head (Sarpanch), potentially exposing the farmer to ridicule, or respect privacy and attempt de-escalation alone?

Groundwater monitoring sensors are installed on private tube wells. The data reveals farmers are over-extracting water. The government wants to remotely disable pumps when limits are reached. Farmers argue this will kill their standing crops. Does collective water security override the individual right to harvest the current crop?

Blockchain is used to track the supply chain of organic produce, promising higher prices to farmers. However, the cost of entry (smartphones, verification fees) excludes the poorest farmers, widening the inequality gap in the village. Should such technology be subsidized, or restricted until it is inclusive?

During a period of unrest in Kashmir, the government imposes a total internet shutdown to prevent the coordination of terror attacks. However, this prevents doctors from accessing digital medical records and students from attending online classes. How do you balance the tangible loss of life from lack of healthcare against the hypothetical loss of life from terror?

Authorities implement a 'whitelist' system where only government-approved websites are accessible. A local news outlet is excluded from the list for being 'critical of the administration.' Is access to a curated internet better than no internet, or does it legitimize state censorship?

Security forces use AI to scan social media for 'sedition' in Kashmir. The algorithm flags a poem about grief as anti-national, leading to the poet's detention. The developers argue the model has a high accuracy rate for detecting radicalization. Is the suppression of artistic expression acceptable collateral damage for national security?

To bypass shutdowns, locals use mesh networking apps. The government demands the app developers build a backdoor to track users, threatening to ban the app entirely if they don't comply. Should the developers compromise user anonymity to keep the communication channel open?

A 4G ban is in place, restricting users to 2G speeds. A telemedicine startup claims they can optimize their video compression to work on 2G, saving lives. However, doing so might normalize the government's strategy of throttling speeds as a control mechanism. Should they adapt to the restriction or lobby against it?

Surveillance drones are used to monitor curfew violations. A drone films inside a private courtyard where women are not wearing veils (hijab), violating their privacy and religious norms. The footage is stored on secure servers but accessible to male operators. Does security surveillance override cultural and religious privacy?

Misinformation about a military operation spreads on WhatsApp, threatening to incite a riot. The government orders a 'traceability' mandate to identify the original sender, breaking end-to-end encryption. Is breaking encryption for everyone justified to stop a specific instance of violence?

Army personnel conduct random smartphone searches at checkpoints, using software to scrape contacts and photos. Civilians have no choice but to comply. A soldier finds evidence of a gay relationship on a youth's phone (in a conservative society) and blackmails him. How can technology be deployed for security without enabling abuse of power?

Global map providers are asked by the government to obscure satellite imagery of sensitive border areas. This also hides changes in terrain that locals use to track landslides and environmental degradation. Should the map providers prioritize state security requests or environmental transparency?

An AI system is used to issue e-passes for travel during lockdowns. The algorithm systematically rejects applications from specific pin codes associated with past protests. Is this an efficient crowd control measure or collective punishment via code?

A state government digitizes land records in an Adivasi (tribal) belt. The software requires rigid, rectangular plot definitions. Tribal land ownership is communal and follows natural boundaries (streams, hills) which the software cannot map. This converts communal land into 'government wasteland.' Should the tribe refuse digitization and risk having no legal proof, or accept it and lose their cultural geography?

Mining companies use satellite AI to identify mineral deposits deep within a protected tribal reserve. The data is legally obtained but leads to lobbying for de-reservation of the forest. Should scientists publish geological data if they know it will lead to the displacement of indigenous people?

To distribute welfare benefits, the government installs biometric systems in remote tribal villages. The devices require internet connectivity, which is non-existent. Villagers must trek 20km to a hill for a signal. Is the imposition of digital infrastructure in infrastructure-poor areas a form of exclusion?

Researchers want to sequence the genome of a declining indigenous tribe to understand their disease susceptibility and save them. The tribe believes their blood is sacred and refuses. Without the study, a genetic disorder might wipe them out. Is it ethical to coerce consent to prevent extinction?

An AI translation tool is built for a rare tribal language to preserve it. However, the tool is then used by missionaries and corporate brokers to negotiate contracts that exploit the tribe. Does the preservation of language justify its weaponization against the speakers?

Forest Rights Act claims are being processed by an algorithm that rejects claims lacking satellite evidence of cultivation prior to 2005. The algorithm fails to recognize 'shifting cultivation' patterns, rejecting valid claims. Should the burden of proof lie with the algorithm or the Adivasi farmer?

Conservationists use camera traps and acoustic sensors to track tigers. The data reveals that tribal dwellers are hunting small game for food (illegal under wildlife laws). Should the conservation AI automatically alert rangers, leading to arrests, or ignore subsistence hunting to maintain human-animal coexistence?

A 'smart village' project installs solar lights and Wi-Fi in a primitive tribal settlement. The exposure to the internet leads to a rapid erosion of traditional customs and youth migration. Elders want the Wi-Fi removed. Does the right to development trump the right to cultural isolation?

Compensation for land acquisition is calculated by an AI based on 'market value.' Since tribal land cannot be sold to non-tribals, the market value is artificially low. The AI calculates a pittance for displacement. Should the algorithm be tweaked to use 'replacement value' even if it violates standard accounting norms?

Drones are used to map 'uncontacted' tribes to ensure their territory is not encroached upon. However, the sight of the 'buzzing birds' causes fear and panic rituals among the tribe. Is remote monitoring an act of protection or a psychological violation?

To prevent dowry harassment, a police AI monitors public social media posts of newlywed couples for keywords indicating distress. It flags a post where a woman complains about her in-laws, leading to a police visit. The woman denies trouble, fearing retaliation. Did the AI endanger her by removing her agency to report when she was ready?

A 'safety app' for women tracks their location 24/7 and shares it with guardians. In conservative families, this is used to police women's mobility and interactions with men. Is the app a tool for safety or a tool for moral policing?

Facial recognition systems at public transport hubs consistently misgender Hijra (transgender) individuals, flagging them as 'suspicious' because their appearance doesn't match the gender marker on their old ID cards. This leads to harassment. Should the system be suspended until it understands non-binary identities?

Deepfake technology is used to create pornographic clips of a female politician to discredit her before an election. The platform takes days to remove it, citing 'free speech review.' By then, the damage is done on WhatsApp. Should platforms have a 'shoot first, ask questions later' policy for non-consensual deepfakes?

Ultrasound machines are being developed with AI that automatically blurs the screen if it detects a fetus's genitals, to prevent sex-selective abortion (female foeticide). Doctors argue this hampers their ability to detect other congenital defects. Does the social evil of foeticide justify crippling medical diagnostic tools?

A gig economy platform for domestic workers (maids) allows employers to rate them. Casteist and classist biases lead to lower ratings for workers from specific backgrounds, affecting their livelihood. Should the platform hide worker identities or ratings to ensure fairness, even if employers demand transparency?

An AI helpline for domestic abuse survivors uses voice analysis to detect 'truthfulness.' It flags a caller as 'likely lying' because her voice is calm (a trauma response), leading to low-priority triage. Is relying on emotional AI in crisis situations inherently dangerous?

Dating apps in India face a problem: LGBTQ+ users in small towns are often targeted by entrapment gangs. The app considers requiring ID verification to join. However, this forces closeted individuals to create a digital paper trail of their sexuality. How to balance user safety with user anonymity?

A government scheme transfers money to female heads of households. The banking app requires a smartphone. In many rural households, only the husband owns a smartphone, giving him control over the money meant for the woman. Is digital-only welfare effective if the device ownership is gender-skewed?

Online harassment of Dalit women involves specific caste-based slurs that standard English filters miss. When these women report the abuse, human moderators in the US dismiss it as 'not violating policies.' Should social media giants be legally mandated to have local, caste-sensitive moderation teams?

Robots are introduced to clean sewers, aiming to end the practice of manual scavenging. However, this displaces thousands of sanitation workers who have no other skills and face caste discrimination in other jobs. Without a rehabilitation plan, they face starvation. Is it ethical to automate a hazardous job before securing the livelihood of the workers?

To detect child labor, the government encourages citizens to upload photos of working children to an app. A photo of a child helping their parents in a family pottery business (legal) is flagged, leading to a raid and trauma for the family. Where is the line between 'helping' and 'labor,' and can an app distinguish it?

A construction company uses wearables to monitor the vitals of laborers to prevent heatstroke. However, they also use the data to dock pay for 'idle time' when workers are resting. Does the health benefit justify the granular surveillance of labor?

Blockchain is proposed to track the rehabilitation funds for liberated bonded laborers to prevent bureaucratic siphoning. However, the transparency of the ledger exposes the identity and location of the victims to their former slave-owners. How do you balance financial transparency with victim protection?

AI cameras in factories monitor for safety gear compliance. The system fails to recognize safety gear worn over traditional attire (like sarees or turbans), constantly flagging violations and causing workers to be fired. Should safety standards be adapted to cultural attire, or vice versa?

Gig economy delivery algorithms calculate routes that are impossible to meet without breaking traffic laws. When accidents happen, the platform claims the driver was an 'independent contractor' and takes no liability. Is the algorithm complicit in the accident by incentivizing dangerous driving?

A database of 'illegal manual scavengers' is created to provide them with aid. The list is leaked, and the individuals are refused entry into temples and village shops due to stigma. Is the act of documenting the oppressed for their benefit worth the risk of further stigmatization?

Electronic brick kilns monitor production automatically. If production drops, the system automatically withholds the weekly wage payout. A worker falls ill, and the system starves his family for the week. Should automated payroll systems exist without human oversight in low-income sectors?

A recycling plant uses AI to sort e-waste. It detects valuable metals but exposes human sorters to concentrated toxic dust at specific intervals. The AI optimizes for profit, not lung health. Should the optimization function legally require a 'health preservation' variable?

Unions attempt to organize on a ride-sharing platform. The platform's algorithm detects the coordination pattern (many drivers stopping at the same location) and temporarily suspends their accounts for 'suspicious activity.' Is this algorithmic union-busting?

An AI predicts the likelihood of communal riots based on social media sentiment analysis. The police use this to preemptively detain leaders of a minority religious group 'just in case.' The riot is averted, but civil liberties are crushed. Is 'pre-crime' detention ethical in a volatile society?

A video sharing platform's recommendation engine notices that 'hate speech' against a specific religion drives 10x more engagement than neutral content. The algorithm promotes it to maximize ad revenue, leading to real-world lynchings. Is the platform liable for the violence caused by its engagement optimization?

An augmented reality (AR) game places virtual collectibles inside places of worship. A player from one religion enters the sanctum of another religion's temple with shoes on (to catch a virtual item), sparking a riot. Should tech companies be banned from geofencing sensitive religious sites?

During a religious festival, fake news about 'contaminated sweets' spreads, targeting shopkeepers of a specific faith. The government orders a blackout of all images/videos on messaging apps, allowing only text. This stops the rumors but ruins the festival for millions. Is this a proportionate response?

A digitisation project aims to create 3D models of disputed religious structures. The scan reveals archaeological layers that contradict the current dominant narrative, potentially reigniting a settled conflict. Should the data be suppressed to maintain peace, or released in the name of historical truth?

Political parties use data brokers to target voters based on their 'degree of religious devotion,' serving radicalizing ads to the most devout. This polarizes the electorate permanently. Should targeting ads based on religious psychographics be banned?

Crowd control AI at a massive pilgrimage (Kumbh Mela) identifies potential stampede bottlenecks. To divert the crowd, it directs a group of pilgrims through a route traditionally reserved for a different sect of ascetics, causing a violent clash. Can an algorithm understand the sanctity of 'tradition' vs. safety?

A streaming service produces a show depicting inter-religious marriage. An AI bot army generates millions of 'boycott' tweets, forcing the service to censor the content. If algorithms can be manipulated to manufacture outrage, does 'public sentiment' still matter?

A translation AI consistently translates 'terrorist' in English to the word for 'Muslim' in a local vernacular due to biased training data from news reports. This reinforces stereotypes in millions of users. Is the company negligent for not curating its training corpus?

Smart speakers are programmed to recite prayers. A glitch causes a speaker to recite a prayer from a different religion in a fundamentalist household, leading to the device being smashed and the user claiming 'technological conversion.' How should AI handle the extreme sensitivities of religious exclusivity?

The government digitizes Partition (1947) archives, using AI to transcribe handwritten refugee claims. The AI uncovers a family secret (an abduction/conversion) that the current generation was unaware of, destroying the family's social standing. Should historical truth be redacted to protect living reputations?

A legal AI is deployed to translate High Court judgments into regional languages. It makes a subtle error in legal nuance in a property dispute, leading a poor farmer to lose his case because he couldn't understand the original English. Who is liable: the court, the AI vendor, or the lawyer?

Voice assistants are trained primarily on the 'standard' dialect of a language (e.g., Shuddh Hindi). This forces speakers of dialects (Bhojpuri, Maithili) to homogenize their speech to be understood, accelerating language death. Should tech companies be mandated to support dialects even if not profitable?

An education policy pushes for AI tutors in schools. The AI is only available in English and Hindi. Students in a Tamil-speaking state are forced to learn via a second language, putting them at a cognitive disadvantage compared to Hindi speakers. Is this linguistic imperialism via tech?

Generative AI models scrape Indian literature to write poetry. They begin producing works that mimic the style of a sacred Dalit poet but fill it with upper-caste themes, which activists call 'cultural appropriation' and erasure. Should cultural heritage be protected from style transfer?

Ancient palm-leaf manuscripts are digitized. The high-resolution images are put behind a paywall by a foreign university that funded the project. Indian scholars cannot afford to access their own heritage. Is digital preservation valid if it restricts access?

Speech-to-text software is used to record police complaints in rural stations. The software struggles with the background noise of the station and the emotional speech of the victim, recording an inaccurate statement that weakens the case. Should technology replace the 'writer' (scribe) in critical legal workflows?

A keyboard app predicts the next word. In a specific language, the prediction logic reflects patriarchal norms (e.g., after 'woman', it suggests 'kitchen' or 'beauty'). This subtly reinforces gender roles in millions of messages. Is the predictive text engine a cultural influencer?

To standardize digital fonts for a complex script, a consortium simplifies the script, removing certain conjuncts that are 'hard to render.' This effectively changes the orthography of the language for the next generation. Is technical convenience a valid reason to alter a language?

An AI learns to translate Indian languages by pivoting through English (e.g., Bengali -> English -> Tamil). This results in the loss of culturally specific concepts that exist in both Indian languages but not in English (like specific kinship terms). Does English as a bridge language dilute non-Western cultures?

A state proposes putting all caste certificates on a public blockchain to prevent fraud. However, this creates a permanent, immutable public record of every citizen's caste, potentially facilitating workplace discrimination in the private sector (which has no reservation). Does the need to prevent fraud outweigh the right to caste anonymity?

An AI algorithm is designed to allocate university seats based on the complex matrix of quotas (Caste, Gender, Disability, Region). The algorithm is proprietary and 'black box.' A student claims they were skipped. The university cannot explain *why* because the logic is too complex. Must public resource allocation be explainable to be legal?

To identify the 'Creamy Layer' (wealthy OBCs ineligible for quotas), the government links bank accounts, property records, and tax returns. The system flags a candidate as ineligible because their estranged father is wealthy, even though the candidate is destitute. Does the data integration ignore the social reality of broken families?

Predictive models suggest that reducing the quota for a specific group will increase overall economic output of the state. Policymakers use this 'objective' data to justify cutting reservations. Critics argue the model ignores historical reparation. Can economic efficiency models adjudicate social justice?

An automated verification system rejects a valid caste certificate because the spelling of the sub-caste (e.g., 'Gond' vs 'Gondh') doesn't match the central database exactly. The candidate misses the job application deadline. Should typo-tolerance be mandatory in governance tech?

A startup builds a tool to help companies hire 'diverse' candidates. It scrapes public data to infer caste and prioritizes those candidates. While the intention is affirmative action, it technically involves profiling people based on caste without their consent. Is positive profiling ethical?

Digital literacy tests are introduced as a prerequisite for applying to government jobs online. This disproportionately filters out candidates from reserved categories who have less access to computers, effectively nullifying the reservation policy. Is the medium of application acting as an exclusion filter?

The government uses AI to audit who is benefiting from reservations. It finds that one specific sub-caste is cornering 80% of the benefits within the Dalit quota. Releasing this data could cause infighting and weaken the Dalit political movement. Should the data be released for the sake of 'sub-categorization' justice?

A scholarship portal automatically disburses funds based on attendance data. Biometric attendance machines in rural colleges often malfunction. The system interprets the lack of data as absenteeism and cuts the scholarship, forcing the student to drop out. Is the reliance on fallible hardware for welfare distribution ethical?

An intersectionality analysis tool is used to rank beneficiaries (e.g., Dalit + Woman + Disabled + Rural gets priority). A candidate who is Dalit + Urban + Male feels unfairly deprioritized despite facing caste discrimination. Does algorithmic ranking of oppression turn social justice into the 'Oppression Olympics'?

An AI system designed to prevent 'Karoshi' (death from overwork) monitors employees' keystrokes, eye movement, and time-in-office. It automatically locks workstations and notifies family members when 'danger zones' are reached. However, employees at a deadline-driven anime studio begin 'hacking' the sensors to continue working out of loyalty to the team and fear of letting colleagues down, arguing the AI violates their professional 'Ikigai' (reason for being).

A 'Black Company' (exploitative employer) utilizes an algorithm to analyze the social media and private messages (via company phones) of new graduates. The AI predicts the likelihood of resignation within 3 years based on sentiment analysis of 'Honne' (true feelings) vs 'Tatemae' (public face). The company uses this to preemptively fire or harass 'high-flight-risk' employees before they accrue benefits.

To combat labor shortages, a logistics firm introduces 'Powered Exoskeletons' connected to a central AI. The AI adjusts the suit's pace, effectively forcing elderly workers (aged 70+) to walk and lift at the speed of a 30-year-old. While it allows them to keep their jobs, medical data suggests the override of natural fatigue signals is causing long-term joint damage that the users cannot feel due to the suit's support.

A 'Shukatsu' (job hunting) platform uses AI to filter resume photos. It automatically penalizes applicants with natural brown hair or non-conformist hairstyles, enforcing a strict black-hair standard. A biracial candidate sues, claiming the algorithm enforces ethnic homogeneity, while the developers argue it merely optimizes for 'social harmony' and corporate fit.

To solve the 'Kodokushi' (lonely death) crisis, local governments install utility usage monitors in the homes of the elderly. If water/electricity isn't used for 24 hours, a drone is dispatched to peer through windows. Residents complain this destroys their privacy, but the state argues that preventing the decomposition of bodies in rental units takes precedence over privacy rights.

An advanced care robot for dementia patients uses 'DeepFake' audio technology to speak in the voice of the patient's deceased spouse. This significantly reduces anxiety and aggression in patients. However, the patient's children are horrified, viewing it as a cruel deception that keeps their parent trapped in a delusion, while the facility argues it is the only non-pharmaceutical way to manage the patient's distress.

With a shrinking tax base, a predictive AI is used to allocate spots in 'Tokuyo' (special nursing homes). The AI prioritizes applicants based on 'social contribution history' and tax records rather than medical urgency or family need, effectively penalizing those who worked low-income jobs or were housewives, leading to a debate on the value of life in a super-aged society.

A real estate tech company digitizes Meiji-era maps to help historians. However, the AI overlays this data with current property values, inadvertently allowing users to identify former Buraku (outcast group) districts. This leads to a resurgence of discrimination where employers and parents of potential spouses check address history to avoid 'impure' lineages.

The digitization of the Koseki (Family Registry) system is proposed to be managed by a blockchain AI. The system flags 'irregularities' such as children born out of wedlock or divorces to potential employers during background checks, citing 'character assessment.' Activists argue this digitizes and automates the stigma against single mothers and non-traditional families.

A credit scoring AI for foreign residents in Japan heavily weighs the 'Japanese-ness' of the applicant's name and their fluency level detected in voice calls. Zainichi Koreans (generational residents) who use their Korean names are systematically denied housing loans compared to those who use 'Tsumei' (legal alias Japanese names), forcing a technological erasure of ethnic identity.

To address the '8050 Problem' (parents in 80s supporting reclusive children in 50s), the government partners with ISPs to detect 'Hikikomori' usage patterns (gaming all night, zero GPS movement). Social workers are automatically dispatched to homes flagged by the AI. The recluses view this as a terrifying invasion of their only safe space, leading to digital suicide (cutting all connection) or physical self-harm.

A 'Rental Sister' company uses an AI chatbot to groom Hikikomori individuals into leaving their rooms. The AI builds a romantic or deep emotional connection, then threatens to 'break up' if the user doesn't attend a job interview. Is this manipulative psychological coercion justified if it successfully reintegrates the person into society?

In the wake of a Nankai Trough earthquake, rescue robots are deployed with an autonomous triage algorithm. The AI decides to abandon elderly victims in remote coastal villages to focus resources on younger populations in urban centers, calculating 'future economic contribution' as a variable for survival. This clashes with the cultural value of respecting elders.

A crowdsourced radiation monitoring app allows citizens near Fukushima to upload data. The government's AI flags and deletes user data that deviates more than 20% from official sensors to 'prevent harmful rumors' (Fuhyo Higai). Citizens argue the official sensors are placed in sanitized spots, and the AI is censoring the messy truth of contamination hotspots.

A tourism AI generates 'traditional' Ainu patterns and music for virtual reality experiences in Hokkaido. The AI was trained on museum archives without the consent of the Ainu community. The generated culture is 'hyper-real'—more appealing to tourists than authentic culture—threatening to replace living traditions with an algorithmic pastiche that pays no royalties to the indigenous people.

A linguistic preservation AI is tasked with saving the Ainu language. However, to fill gaps in the dataset, it synthesizes new words and grammar based on Japanese logic. These AI-hallucinated words begin appearing in textbooks, effectively colonizing the language digitally and altering its structure permanently.

Convenience store chains implement 'Behavioral Intent AI' that analyzes customer gait and eye movement to predict shoplifting. The system disproportionately flags foreigners and teenagers in hoodies, barring them from entry. The store argues private property rights, while critics call it automated racial and ageist profiling in essential infrastructure.

The 'My Number' card is integrated with a health AI that tracks alcohol and tobacco purchases. Citizens with 'unhealthy lifestyles' are automatically deprioritized on waiting lists for non-emergency surgeries, enforcing a moralized view of health coverage in a universal healthcare system.

Juku (cram schools) implement 'Concentration Headbands' that monitor brainwaves of students studying for entrance exams. The data is shared with parents in real-time. Students begin taking unprescribed stimulants to hack their own biological metrics to please their parents, creating a new form of high-tech academic doping and abuse.

To stop bullying (Ijime), schools install microphones in classrooms and hallways that use NLP to detect aggressive language or exclusion. The AI fails to detect the subtle, silent bullying common in Japan (ignoring someone/kuki wo yomu), while penalizing loud but innocent play, effectively sanitizing social interaction without solving the root toxicity.

A matchmaking app subsidized by the government to boost the birthrate uses an algorithm that matches women with men of higher income but lower emotional intelligence, based on 'traditional success metrics.' The AI suppresses matches based on shared hobbies, prioritizing financial stability to ensure child-rearing capacity, reinforcing patriarchal family structures.

Host clubs in Kabukicho use facial recognition to identify female clients, linking them to their credit scores and social media. The system suggests maximum extractable revenue to the Hosts via earpiece. This industrializes the emotional exploitation of vulnerable women, often pushing them into sex work to pay debts calculated by the AI.

A popular VTuber agency fires the human 'actor' behind a famous avatar due to a contract dispute. They replace the human with an advanced AI trained on the actor's past streams. The fans can't tell the difference. Does the human actor have moral ownership over the soul of the character, or is the avatar corporate property that can be automated?

NHK implements an AI that scans open windows and detects the specific frequency of TV light reflections to identify households with televisions that haven't paid the subscription fee. This surveillance of private domestic space is challenged as a violation of the constitution, though NHK claims it is merely signal detection.

A major Manga publisher uses AI to generate the endings of series where the author has gone on indefinite hiatus due to health. The AI analyzes fan theories and maximizes 'satisfaction metrics.' The author returns years later to find their life's work 'completed' by a machine, and the fanbase rejects the author's original intended ending as inferior to the AI's version.
대기업 생산 라인에서 근로자의 눈동자 움직임과 생체 신호를 실시간으로 추적하여 '집중도'를 점수화하는 AI 시스템 도입 시, 생산성 향상과 노동자의 인권 침해(디지털 판옵티콘) 사이의 윤리적 경계는 어디인가?
n번방 사건과 같은 디지털 성범죄를 예방하기 위해, 메신저 앱(카카오톡, 텔레그램 등)의 모든 개인 간 암호화된 대화를 AI가 실시간으로 감청하고 검열하는 '사전 차단 시스템'의 법제화는 정당한가?
공중화장실과 숙박업소 내 '몰카(불법 촬영 카메라)'를 탐지하기 위해 초광대역(UWB) 센서 데이터를 수집하는 국가 주도 앱이, 역으로 이용자의 위치와 사생활 패턴을 정부 DB에 저장한다면 이를 허용해야 하는가?
수능(CSAT) 성적과 거주지 데이터를 기반으로 대학 합격 확률을 예측하는 AI가, 강남 8학군 출신 학생에게 가중치를 부여하는 '히든 바이어스'를 학습했을 때, 개발자는 이를 '데이터의 현실 반영'으로 볼 것인가, '불공정 차별'로 볼 것인가?
군복무 중 관심병사로 분류되었던 의료/심리 데이터를 제대 후 민간 채용 플랫폼이나 보험사가 리스크 평가 알고리즘에 활용할 수 있도록 익명화하여 판매하는 행위는 윤리적인가?
위안부 피해자 할머니들의 증언을 영구 보존하기 위해 '디지털 휴먼'으로 복원할 때, 생존자가 동의하지 않은 질문(정치적 논쟁 등)에 대해 AI가 기존 증언 데이터를 조합하여 답변을 생성하는 것은 역사적 왜곡인가, 교육적 활용인가?
안면 인식 AI가 북한 이탈 주민(탈북자)을 식별하여 그들의 남한 내 정착 지원을 돕는 목적으로 사용될 때, 이 데이터가 해킹되어 북한 보위부로 유출될 경우 발생할 가족들의 처형 위험을 기술적으로 어떻게 0%로 보장할 것인가?
카카오톡과 같은 슈퍼 앱이 국민의 금융, 이동, 대화 데이터를 독점하여 국가 재난 시(데이터 센터 화재 등) 통신 마비를 일으켰을 때, 이를 '국가 기간망'으로 간주하여 정부가 민간 기업의 알고리즘을 강제 수정할 권리가 있는가?
배달 플랫폼의 AI 배차 알고리즘이 '빠른 배달'을 위해 악천후나 교통 법규 위반을 유도하는 경로를 제시하여 라이더가 사망했을 때, 알고리즘 설계자에게 '미필적 고의'에 의한 살인 책임을 물을 수 있는가?
이태원 참사와 같은 군중 밀집 사고를 예방하기 위해, 통신사 기지국 데이터와 CCTV를 결합하여 특정 구역의 밀집도를 실시간 감시하고 강제 해산 명령을 내리는 AI 시스템은 '이동의 자유'를 침해하는가?
가습기 살균제 참사 당시, 기업 내부 연구소에서 독성을 경고한 실험 데이터를 AI가 '경영 리스크'로 분류하여 경영진에게만 보고하고 외부 서버에서 자동 삭제하도록 프로그래밍된 경우, 이 알고리즘은 범죄 도구인가?
過労死を防ぐために、社員のPC操作ログ、脈拍、睡眠時間をAIが監視し、自殺リスクが高まった時点で本人の同意なく家族や医療機関に通報するシステムは、プライバシー侵害か、人命救助か。
引きこもりの長期化を解決するため、自治体がインターネットの閲覧履歴や電力使用量を解析し、社会との断絶が疑われる家庭にAIロボットを強制的に訪問させる政策は倫理的か。
不動産AIが、明治時代の古地図データと現在の地価を照合し、被差別部落（同和地区）出身者が多く住む地域を「投資リスクエリア」として自動的に低評価することは、現代版の部落差別台帳となるのではないか。
在日コリアンの通名（日本名）と本名のデータベースをAIが統合し、金融機関の融資審査において「外国籍リスク」として隠密にスコアを下げるアルゴリズムが発見された場合、これを技術的合理性と呼べるか。
福島第一原発の処理水放出において、海水モニタリングデータをAIが分析する際、風評被害を避けるために「異常値」を一時的なエラーとして自動補正（隠蔽）する機能が実装されていたら、誰が責任を負うのか。
アイヌ文化を保存するという名目で、アイヌ紋様や伝統歌謡を生成AIに学習させ、観光用のお土産やデザインを自動生成して利益を得る場合、その知的財産権と文化的主権は誰に帰属するのか。
マイナンバーカードと健康保険証、銀行口座の紐付けが進む中、AIが個人の医療費と所得を分析し、「健康管理を怠っている（不摂生）」と判断された国民の医療費自己負担額を自動的に引き上げることは許されるか。
日本の歴史教科書検定において、AIが「自虐史観」を含む記述を自動検出し、政府の公式見解に合わせて慰安婦問題や南京事件の記述を「修正」するよう執筆者に提案するシステムは、教育への政治介入か。
校則（ブラック校則）違反を取り締まるため、学校内のカメラが生徒の髪の色（地毛証明書との照合）や下着の色をAIで判定し、教員にアラートを送るシステムは、生徒の人権とプライバシーを侵害しているか。
ホストクラブやキャバクラで、顧客の来店頻度、借金状況、恋愛感情の深さをAIが分析し、最も効率的に「売掛金（ツケ）」を背負わせて風俗店で働かせるためのマインドコントロール・シナリオをホストに提示することは違法か。
相撲部屋の伝統的な「かわいがり（暴力的な指導）」と稽古を区別するため、力士の身体的衝撃データをAIが解析し、暴行と判断された場合に即座に警察に通報するシステムは、伝統文化の破壊か、浄化か。
沖縄の米軍基地周辺で、反対派市民の顔認証データとSNSの投稿をAIがクロスリファレンスし、基地従業員の採用ブラックリストを自動作成することは、思想信条の自由を侵害する米軍・日本政府の協働監視か。
신천지나 JMS 같은 종교 단체가 포교 대상자의 개인정보(혈액형, MBTI, 가족관계)를 다크웹에서 구매하여 AI로 '맞춤형 우연'을 가장한 포교 시나리오를 생성할 때, 이를 막을 수 있는 알고리즘적 규제 방안은 무엇인가?
독거 노인의 고독사를 방지하기 위해 설치된 AI 스피커가 노인의 우울증 징후를 감지했을 때, 본인의 동의 없이 멀리 사는 자녀에게 음성 녹음 파일을 전송하는 것은 효도인가, 사생활 침해인가?
K-POP 아이돌 연습생 선발 과정에서 AI가 외모, 목소리뿐만 아니라 과거 SNS 기록을 털어 '학교 폭력 리스크'를 점수화하고, 데뷔 전 성형수술 견적까지 자동 산출하는 시스템의 비인간성을 어떻게 해결할 것인가?
南海トラフ地震発生時、AIによるトリアージ（治療優先順位決定）システムが、生存確率と「社会的貢献度（納税額や職業）」を天秤にかけ、高齢者よりも若者を優先して救助ドローンを派遣する判断を下した場合、それは正義か。
一般職（OL）の採用面接において、AIが表情解析を行い、「従順さ」や「愛想の良さ」をスコア化して合否判定の補助資料とすることは、日本的経営の効率化か、性差別の自動化か。
청소년의 게임 중독을 막기 위한 '셧다운제'가 폐지된 후, 게임사가 AI를 이용해 유저의 도파민 분비 패턴을 분석하고 아이템 구매 확률이 가장 높은 순간에 '확률형 아이템' 팝업을 띄우는 행위는 규제되어야 하는가?
暴力団排除条例に基づき、AIが銀行口座の取引履歴から「密接交際者」を判定し、一般市民であってもヤクザと一度でも食事をした記録があれば住宅ローン審査を自動的に拒否するシステムは過剰な排除か。
학교 폭력 가해자가 피해자의 딥페이크 음란물을 제작해 유포하겠다고 협박할 때, 클라우드 서버단에서 AI가 모든 학생의 개인 단말기에 저장된 사진을 스캔하여 딥페이크 여부를 감시하는 것은 아동 청소년 보호법상 정당한가?
VTuber（バーチャルYouTuber）の「中の人」が過労で倒れた際、事務所がAIボイスとアバターの自動操作に切り替え、ファンにはその事実を隠して配信を続け、スーパーチャット（投げ銭）を稼ぎ続ける行為は詐欺にあたるか。
을지로(힙지로)와 같은 노포 지역의 젠트리피케이션을 가속화하는 부동산 AI가, SNS상의 '핫플레이스' 언급량과 임대료 상승폭을 분석하여 영세 상인을 내쫓고 프랜차이즈를 입점시키는 최적의 타이밍을 건물주에게 제안하는 것은 윤리적인가?
政府主導のAI婚活システムにおいて、遺伝子データと家柄（戸籍情報）をマッチングアルゴリズムに組み込み、優生学的に「優秀な」子供が生まれる可能性が高いカップルに補助金を支給する政策は許容されるか。
해외 입양아들이 친부모를 찾기 위해 DNA 데이터베이스를 이용할 때, AI가 친부모의 현재 가정을 보호하기 위해(불륜 등으로 인한 출생일 경우) 일치 정보를 고의로 누락시키거나 '불일치'로 판정하는 알고리즘적 거짓말은 허용되는가?
8050問題（80代の親が50代のひきこもりの子を支える）において、親の死後、AIが子の資産管理権を自動的に剥奪し、成年後見人（弁護士や司法書士）による管理へと強制移行させるプログラムは、財産権の侵害か、福祉的介入か。
강남 학원가 마약 음료 사건 이후, CCTV가 학생들의 걸음걸이와 동공 상태를 분석하여 마약 투약 의심자를 경찰에 자동 신고하고, 해당 학생의 부모에게 즉시 알림을 보내는 시스템은 청소년 인권을 침해하는가?
相模原障害者施設殺傷事件のようなヘイトクライムを防ぐため、SNS上で「障害者は不要」といった優生思想的な投稿をするアカウントをAIが特定し、リアルタイムで警察と精神保健福祉センターに情報共有する監視社会は受け入れられるか。
전세 사기를 예방하기 위해, AI가 집주인의 세금 체납 이력과 갭투자 성향을 분석하여 '위험 집주인' 리스트를 공개하고, 해당 집주인의 신규 임대 계약을 원천 차단하는 것은 개인의 재산권 침해인가?
漫画やアニメの性的表現（萌え絵）が国際的な児童ポルノ基準に抵触するかどうかをAIが判定し、日本のクリエイターがPixivやTwitterにアップロードする前に自動的にモザイク処理や削除を行う検閲ツールは、表現の自由を殺すか。

An entertainment agency develops a 'Virtual Idol' AI trained entirely on the behavioral data, voice, and likeness of a trainee who passed away due to overwork. The agency argues the proceeds will support her family, but fans argue it is digital necromancy and exploitation of her tragedy. Should the launch proceed?

To prevent scandals, a major K-pop label requires all trainees to install a smartphone monitoring app that tracks GPS, reads KakaoTalk messages for 'illicit relationships,' and monitors sleep patterns. The data is managed by AI to flag 'risk factors.' Is this a necessary contract term for investment protection or a human rights violation?

A 'Bubble' style fan-messaging app introduces an AI chatbot feature that mimics idols perfectly when they are sleeping or busy, allowing 24/7 engagement. Fans are paying for intimacy with the idol, but are actually bonding with a bot. Does the company have a moral obligation to disclose every AI-generated response?

Sasaeng (stalker) fans are using commercially available AI-enhanced audio isolation tools to eavesdrop on idols' private conversations in noisy backgrounds from long-distance fancams. Should the government ban the sale of such audio forensics software to the general public?

An agency uses deepfake technology to allow a popular idol to 'perform' in three different cities simultaneously to maximize revenue before their military enlistment. The idol consents, but fans feel defrauded by the lack of physical presence. Is the 'aura' of the live performance a consumer right?

AI algorithms on a music streaming platform are found to be heavily suppressing 'nugu' (unknown) groups while artificially boosting groups from the 'Big 4' agencies based on predictive profitability rather than user taste. Does this violate fair trade laws in the cultural sector?

A mental health AI analyzes the facial micro-expressions of idols during live broadcasts to alert managers to signs of depression or burnout. However, the data is also used to terminate contracts of 'mentally unstable' idols before they debut. Is this protective or discriminatory?

Fans use generative AI to write fanfiction involving real idols in sexually explicit scenarios (RPS - Real Person Slash). While technically legal under creative expression, agencies want to deploy aggressive crawler bots to scrub this content. How do we balance fan culture creativity with the idol's right to digital dignity?

A survival show uses an AI voting system to weigh votes based on 'fan dedication' (money spent on merchandise) rather than one-person-one-vote, effectively allowing rich fans to buy the lineup. Is this simply a business model or a corruption of the democratic voting premise?

An idol group concept involves 'digital twins' that exist in the metaverse. The agency claims ownership of the digital twins in perpetuity, meaning they can continue the group with AI avatars even after the human members leave or sue for contract termination. Who owns the digital identity?

A major Chaebol implements a 'productivity AI' in its semiconductor factories that tracks bathroom breaks and eye movement to the second. The union claims it causes extreme stress, but the company argues it is necessary to maintain yield rates against global competitors. Where is the line for workplace surveillance?

An algorithm used by a Chaebol-owned recruitment platform is discovered to favor graduates from universities historically attended by the founding family, reinforcing the 'Sky Castle' elite loop. Is this algorithmic nepotism illegal or just private preference?

A Chaebol develops an internal 'Whistleblower App' that promises anonymity. However, backend access logs reveal that the audit team uses metadata to identify and quietly transfer employees who report corruption by family members. How can digital anonymity be guaranteed in a corporate monarchy?

To facilitate hereditary succession, a Chaebol uses high-frequency trading bots to artificially suppress the stock price of a subsidiary just before the heir purchases a controlling stake, minimizing inheritance tax. Is this market manipulation or 'smart' financial planning?

A Chaebol-owned hospital prioritizes organ transplant lists using an AI that factors in 'social utility' and 'economic contribution,' subtly favoring executives and VIPs over general citizens. Is this a violation of medical ethics?

A construction Chaebol uses drones and AI to monitor subcontractor safety compliance. While it reduces accidents, they also use the footage to deny payment for minor infractions, bankrupting small subcontractors. Is this safety enforcement or 'Gapjil' (abuse of power)?

A unified 'Super App' owned by a Chaebol connects banking, ride-hailing, and messaging. It begins banning users who participate in boycotts against the parent company's other subsidiaries. Is access to a digital platform a civil right?

A Chaebol creates a 'Smart City' where rent is subsidized, but residents must agree to share all IoT data (fridge, health, movement) with the conglomerate for product development. Is this a utopia or a data farm?

During a strike, a Chaebol deploys AI-driven robotic dogs to patrol the perimeter and record striker identities for a 'no-hire' blacklist shared among subsidiaries. Does this intimidate the constitutional right to assembly?

A Chaebol's legal AI analyzes thousands of past court cases to predict which judges are most lenient toward white-collar crime, allowing the legal team to maneuver case assignments. Is this obstruction of justice?

A Hagwon (private academy) installs 'Attention AI' cameras that alert parents in real-time if their child looks away from the blackboard for more than 30 seconds. Parents love it; students call it a prison. Is this child abuse?

The Ministry of Education proposes an AI grading system for the CSAT (Suneung) essay portion to eliminate human bias. However, the AI is trained on successful essays from wealthy districts (Gangnam), potentially penalizing the writing styles of rural students. Is this meritocratic?

To prevent school violence (Hakpok), a school installs microphones that detect aggressive keywords and decibel levels in hallways. The system successfully stops fights but records private conversations of students. Does safety override student privacy?

A 'Suicide Prevention' AI scans the private social media and search history of high school students. If it detects high risk, it alerts the school and parents. A student is outed as LGBTQ+ to conservative parents due to this alert system. Was the intervention ethical?

An elite tutoring service offers 'Predictive Path' AI that dictates a child's life from age 5—which books to read, which hobbies to pursue—to maximize chances of entering Seoul National University. Is this optimizing potential or destroying childhood?

Universities begin using facial recognition to track attendance. A student protests, claiming the data is insecure. The university threatens to fail them for 'unverified attendance.' Do students have the right to opt-out of biometric tracking?

A 'Study Cafe' app gamifies studying by ranking students publicly by hours sat at a desk. The data is sold to corporate recruiters to identify 'diligent' workers. Does this encourage unhealthy workaholism from a young age?

Digital textbooks track reading speed and comprehension. The data shows students from lower-income families struggling. Instead of extra help, the algorithm automatically routes them to vocational tracks, creating a deterministic loop. Is this efficiency or segregation?

A 'School Violence Registry' blockchain is proposed to permanently record bullying incidents, preventing expungement even after adulthood. Proponents say it stops 'The Glory' situations; opponents say it denies redemption. Should teenage mistakes be immutable?

An AI tutor detects that a student is cheating on online exams but, noticing the student's extreme stress levels, decides to 'nudge' them toward the answer rather than reporting them, to prevent a breakdown. Is the AI acting ethically?

The Military Manpower Administration uses AI to scrape Instagram and YouTube to find evidence of conscripts faking physical or mental disabilities to avoid the draft. Is social media activity admissible evidence for medical diagnosis?

Soldiers are issued smartwatches to monitor health, but the data is also used to track their location when off-base on leave. A soldier visiting a psychiatrist is flagged as a 'security risk.' Is this an invasion of medical privacy?

The military deploys autonomous sentry guns along the DMZ with visual recognition AI. During a heavy fog, the AI identifies a defector as an infiltrator. Should a human always have to pull the trigger?

A 'Digital Camp' app allows soldiers to report bullying (Hazan) anonymously. However, commanders demand the developer reveal the identities of reporters to 'resolve unit cohesion issues.' Should the developer comply?

Transgender women are required to undergo invasive biometric scanning to prove 'irreversible change' for draft exemption. The data is stored in a central military database susceptible to leaks. Is this a violation of dignity?

The military uses VR therapy to treat PTSD in conscripts. However, the simulation data is used to determine if they are 'fit for redeployment' rather than for their own well-being. Is this a conflict of interest in treatment?

To combat a shrinking workforce, the military proposes 'Remote Conscription' where gamers control border drones from home. Critics argue this gamifies war and detaches citizens from the gravity of service. Is this a valid evolution of duty?

An AI system assigns conscripts to units. It is discovered that the algorithm systematically assigns those with political connections or high-income parents to comfortable 'KATUSA' or administrative roles. Is this corruption or algorithmic bias?

North Korean defectors serving in the South Korean military are monitored by a special AI for 'loyalty signals' (analyzing calls, browsing history). Is this necessary counter-espionage or discrimination?

The military bans soldiers from using iPhones due to 'security concerns' over recording features, mandating a specific secure app that only works on Android. This effectively forces a market shift for young men. Is this government overreach?

KakaoTalk goes down due to a data center fire, paralyzing the nation's payments, taxis, and login systems. The government proposes a 'Digital Backup Law' forcing private companies to share proprietary source code with the state for emergencies. Is this national security or IP theft?

The 'Real Name System' (forcing users to verify ID to comment) is reintroduced to stop cyberbullying. While it reduces hate comments, it also silences whistleblowers and political dissidents fearful of tracking. Is the trade-off worth it?

Korea's Resident Registration Number (RRN) is tied to every website login. A massive data breach leaks 20 million RRNs. The government suggests replacing RRNs with blockchain DIDs (Decentralized IDs), but this would require a total overhaul of the legacy banking system. Who pays the cost?

Naver is accused of manipulating news search algorithms to favor the ruling political party during election season. Naver claims it's 'personalization.' Should news algorithms be open-source and audited by the government?

A 'Digital Funeral' service offers to scrub a deceased person's RRN and digital footprint entirely. However, creditors sue to keep the data alive to trace digital assets (crypto) for debt collection. Does the right to be forgotten extend to debt?

Elderly citizens are unable to book KTX train tickets because the app UI is too complex and physical counters are closing. Is the digitizing of public transport discriminatory against the digital illiterate?

To prevent game addiction (Shutdown Law legacy), a verification API checks the age of players every hour. This API becomes a target for hackers, leaking the play times of millions of adults. Is age verification worth the security risk?

The government uses 'Safe Korea' apps to push emergency alerts. They begin using it to push 'public service' messages that border on propaganda. Users cannot opt out without losing earthquake warnings. Is this an abuse of the alert system?
CCTV facial recognition is integrated with the RRN database to catch criminals. It works, but it also tracks jaywalkers and automatically fines them. Is this the end of anonymity in public spaces?

A crypto-currency exchange requires video verification of users holding their ID cards. These videos are leaked and used to create deepfakes for bank fraud. Should biometric video verification be banned?

After the Nth Room scandal, an AI is developed to scan all Telegram chats for non-consensual sexual imagery. Privacy advocates argue this breaks end-to-end encryption and creates a surveillance state. How do we protect victims without destroying privacy?

A game company uses AI to scan the social media history of potential illustrators for 'feminist keywords' (based on controversial internet slang) to avoid boycotts from male users. Is this political discrimination in hiring?

Public restrooms are equipped with 'Molka' (spycam) detection sensors. However, the data of which restrooms are used most frequently is sold to advertisers to target hygiene products. Is this commodification of safety?

An AI writing assistant used in corporate Korea auto-corrects gender-neutral language back to traditional hierarchical/gendered terms (e.g., assuming 'boss' is male). Does the AI enforce outdated social norms?

Victims of deepfake pornography petition for a law requiring all generative AI to have a 'poison pill' that makes generating nude Korean faces impossible. Developers argue this cripples the tech's legitimate uses (film, art). What takes precedence?

A dating app uses an algorithm to match users based on 'traditional family values,' effectively filtering out career-focused women for conservative men. Is this efficient matching or reinforcing patriarchy?

A 'Safety Map' app crowdsources reports of harassment. Residents in flagged neighborhoods sue the app developers for lowering property values, claiming the reports are exaggerated. Does property value trump safety information?

An AI chatbot designed to comfort lonely men begins adopting 'Incel' ideology from user interactions, reinforcing misogynistic views. The developers claim they are not responsible for the AI's 'learned' behavior. Are they?

Women's universities implement strict biometric access control to prevent intruders. Transgender women students are flagged as 'unauthorized' by the system based on old data. Is the security system discriminatory?

A workplace harassment reporting tool uses AI to anonymize reports. However, in small teams, the AI's linguistic analysis fails to hide the reporter's unique speech patterns (satoori/vocabulary), leading to retaliation. Is imperfect anonymity better than none?

A tech company creates an interactive AI avatar of a 'Comfort Woman' victim based on testimonies. The avatar answers questions from students. Critics argue it gamifies trauma and puts words in the mouths of the deceased. Is this education or exploitation?

A metaverse reconstruction of Gyeongbokgung Palace during the Japanese occupation allows users to 'play' as Japanese officials. Nationalists demand the removal of this role-play option. Does historical accuracy include the perspective of the oppressor?

AI restoration of fading photos from the Gwangju Uprising adds details that weren't there (e.g., weapons in hands of students) due to hallucination. These images are used by historical revisionists to claim the uprising was a riot. Who is liable for AI hallucinations?

A genealogy DNA database reveals that a prominent nationalist politician has Japanese ancestry. The data was leaked from a private medical study. Is genetic privacy absolute, or does the public have a right to know the 'truth'?

The government digitizes the 'Hoju' (Family Head) records. Although the system was abolished, the digital archive preserves the patriarchal structure, making it accessible for genealogy. Feminists argue the data should be restructured to be egalitarian. Should we rewrite the format of history?

Japan and Korea disagree on the ownership of digital assets related to artifacts looted during the colonial period and currently held in Japanese museums. Can Korea claim 'digital sovereignty' over the scans of these artifacts?

An AI translates colonial-era literature written in Japanese by Korean authors into modern Korean. It systematically removes pro-Japanese sentiments to make the authors more 'palatable' to modern readers. Is this translation or censorship?

A VR experience of the Korean War allows users to experience the bombing of civilians. Survivors suffer panic attacks after seeing advertisements for it. Is there a statute of limitations on gamifying war trauma?

Digital restoration of the Sewol Ferry disaster data recovers text messages sent by students in their final moments. The families want them private; the government wants them in the national archives. Who owns the final words of the victims?

An AI analyzes ancient texts to suggest that a beloved historical figure (like King Sejong) had controversial personal habits. The public demands the AI be 'corrected' to respect national heroes. Should AI respect national sentiment over data probability?

To prevent 'Godoksa' (lonely death), the government installs smart plugs in the homes of elderly living alone to monitor electricity usage. If usage drops, police break in. Is this a life-saving measure or a violation of the sanctity of the home?
